stories.headline: Alibaba Q4 Revenue Up 3% to $35.3B, Cloud Up 38% as AI Spend Pressures Margins

key_facts.fact: Alibaba reported quarterly revenue of RMB243.38 billion ($35.28B) for the three months ended March 31, 2026, up 3% year-over-year from RMB236.45B; on a like-for-like basis (excluding divested Sun Art and Intime), revenue would have grown 11%.

key_facts.fact: The 12 plugins span commercial, privacy, corporate, employment, product and AI governance, covering document search/review, case-law research, deposition preparation and drafting; they include 'employment counsel', 'litigation associate' and a 'law student' bar-exam tool.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini-Powered 'Magic Pointer' for Chrome and Googlebook

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind published a research blog and experimental demos for an AI-enabled mouse pointer powered by Gemini that aims to understand both what the user is pointing at and why it matters.
key_facts.excerpt: We've been exploring new AI-powered capabilities to help the pointer not only understand what it's pointing at, but also why it matters to the user... Today, we're outlining the underlying principles guiding our thinking on future user interfaces, and sharing experimental demos of an AI-enabled pointer, powered by Gemini.

key_facts.fact: Two interactive demos are live in Google AI Studio: one for editing images by pointing and talking, and one for finding places on a map.
key_facts.excerpt: you could visit Google AI Studio to edit an image or find places on the map, just by pointing and speaking.

key_facts.fact: The pointer is being integrated into Gemini in Chrome — users can select products on a page and ask Gemini to compare, or point to visualize a new couch in their living room — and into the upcoming 'Googlebook' laptop as 'Magic Pointer'.
key_facts.excerpt: We are now integrating these principles to reimagine pointing in Chrome and our new Googlebook laptop experience... Similarly, we'll soon roll out Magic Pointer in Googlebook, allowing users to harness Gemini at their fingertips for a more intuitive experience.

key_facts.fact: Google announced the Magic Pointer alongside Googlebook, a new laptop category 'built from the ground up for Gemini intelligence' set to launch in fall 2026, in partnership with OEMs including Dell and HP.
key_facts.excerpt: We are introducing Googlebook, a new category of laptops built from the ground up for Gemini intelligence. These devices feature the Magic Pointer for contextual suggestions and custom widgets to help you organize your tasks. Keep an eye on googlebook.com for more updates before the devices launch this fall.

stories.headline: Foxconn Confirms North America Factory Cyberattack; Nitrogen Claims 8TB Stolen

key_facts.fact: Foxconn confirmed Tuesday that some of its North American factories suffered a cyberattack and that affected plants are 'currently resuming normal production' after outages.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Some of Foxconn's factories in North America suffered a cyberattack. The cybersecurity team immediately activated the response mechanism and implemented multiple operational measures to ensure the continuity of production and delivery. The affected factories are currently resuming normal production,' Foxconn said.

key_facts.fact: Ransomware group Nitrogen claimed responsibility, posting that it stole 8 terabytes of data — roughly 11 million files — including schematics and project details from Dell, Google, Apple, AMD, Intel, and Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: A ransomware group is attempting to extort the electronics manufacturing giant Foxconn, claiming that it stole 8 terabytes of data from the company, including schematics and project details from customers including Dell, Google, Apple, and Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: The breach centered on Foxconn's Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin facility — a hub for AI server production — where Wi-Fi was cut off May 1 and core plant infrastructure was disrupted; production was halted for roughly a week before resuming May 12.
key_facts.excerpt: On May 11, 2026, the Nitrogen ransomware group claimed to have stolen 8 terabytes of data from Foxconn's Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin facility — over 11 million files including assembly instructions, data center topology diagrams for Google and Intel, and hardware schematics linked to Apple, NVIDIA, and Dell... Outage: Multi-day IT outage began May 1, halting production for nearly a week.

key_facts.fact: Allegedly stolen materials include data center network topology diagrams for Google and Intel — architectural maps of live infrastructure with supply chain intelligence implications.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nitrogen ransomware claim against Foxconn Wisconsin is a supply chain intelligence story, not just a ransomware story. The alleged theft of data center network topology diagrams — architectural maps of live infrastructure — could have consequences far beyond Foxconn itself.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reverses, Joins Trump on China Trip After 11th-Hour Invite

key_facts.fact: Nvidia confirmed CEO Jensen Huang would visit Beijing with Trump after the U.S. president personally called him; Huang flew to Alaska to board Air Force One during a refueling stop.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia confirmed to CNBC that CEO Jensen Huang will visit China this week... After seeing the media coverage of Huang's absence from the delegation, Trump called the Nvidia executive and asked him to join, a source familiar with the situation told CNBC. Huang flew to Alaska to board Air Force One, the source said.

key_facts.fact: The reversal followed reports that Huang had been left off the original White House delegation list of 17 executives released Monday, a smaller group than the 27 who joined Trump's 2017 China trip.
key_facts.excerpt: Seventeen American CEOs were on a list of invited business delegates released by the White House on Monday – a smaller group than Trump's previous China trip in 2017, when 27 high-profile executives joined. Huang was not included on Monday's list, which fuelled speculation Washington had limited appetite for rolling back some of its tech export controls.

key_facts.fact: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk also traveled on Air Force One; Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday and Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House confirmed that Huang had boarded Air Force One during a refuelling stop in Anchorage, Alaska. It added that Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk was also travelling on the presidential plane.

key_facts.fact: Huang's addition revived hopes of progress on Nvidia's stalled sale of H200 AI chips in China; Washington currently lets Nvidia sell the H200 with a 25% revenue surcharge to the U.S. Treasury, with more advanced chips still restricted.
key_facts.excerpt: Huang's last-minute addition to the US delegation comes as Nvidia struggles to export its chips to China. Washington has allowed the firm to sell its H200 graphics processing unit in China as long as a 25 per cent revenue surcharge flows to the US Treasury, but the firm's more advanced models remain restricted.

key_facts.fact: Huang has previously pegged the China AI chip market at $50 billion and told CNBC last week it 'would be a privilege' to accompany Trump.
key_facts.excerpt: Huang, who's pegged China's market for AI chips at $50 billion, told CNBC last week that 'it would be a privilege' to accompany Trump on the trip.

key_facts.fact: Huang has framed the China AI market as a roughly $50 billion opportunity that could reach $200 billion by the end of the decade as global AI demand grows about 50% per year.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang... described China as a $50 billion opportunity that he expects to grow 50% per year, with the potential to reach $200 billion by the end of the decade.

stories.headline: Isomorphic Labs Raises $2.1B Series B Led by Thrive to Scale AI Drug Design

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs, a DeepMind spinout, raised $2.1 billion in a Series B led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet, GV, MGX, Temasek, CapitalG, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund participating.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs was founded in 2021 as a DeepMind spinout, building on AlphaFold; it previously signed drug discovery deals worth up to $3 billion with Eli Lilly and Novartis.

stories.headline: Samsung Pay Talks Collapse After 17 Hours; 50,000+ Workers Set to Strike May 21 for 18 Days

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics and its largest union failed to reach a pay deal after more than 17 hours of marathon talks that ended early Wednesday May 13
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its union failed to reach an agreement on the source of funds for performance bonuses and their institutionalization after more than 17 hours of marathon negotiations at the National Labor Relations Commission that lasted until the early morning of May 13.

key_facts.fact: More than 50,000 unionized workers are expected to strike for 18 days starting May 21, threatening AI chip production
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its South Korean labor union failed to reach a pay deal on Wednesday, its union leader said, expecting over 50,000 workers would go ahead with a full strike that threatens to disrupt production of AI and other chips.

key_facts.fact: The union demands the abolition of the 50%-of-base-salary cap on bonus pay and the allocation of 15% of annual operating profit to the bonus pool
key_facts.excerpt: The union has called for the scrapping of a cap on bonus pay currently set at 50 per cent of annual base salary, the allocation of 15 per cent of annual operating profit to bonus pay and more clarity on how bonus pay is calculated.

key_facts.fact: South Korean Prime Minister Kim Min-seok called an emergency meeting of related ministers, citing the 'gravity of the impact on the national economy'
key_facts.excerpt: Underscoring the angst caused by the potential strike, South Korea called an emergency meeting for related ministers. There, Prime Minister Kim Min-seok instructed the government to closely manage the situation 'considering the gravity of the impact on the national economy'.

key_facts.fact: A walkout could delay shipments to customers, push up chip prices further and benefit rivals such as SK Hynix
key_facts.excerpt: More than 50,000 workers could walk off [...] a move that would likely delay shipments to customers, push up chip prices further and benefit rivals.

key_facts.fact: The union grievance centers on the bonus gap with rival SK Hynix; union representative Choi Seung-ho said no agenda items were addressed
key_facts.excerpt: I would like to express some regret that none of the agenda items requested by the union have been addressed,' union representative Choi Seung-ho told reporters at about 3 a.m. local time on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Meta Employees Protest Model Capability Initiative Surveillance Software Ahead of May 20 Layoffs

key_facts.fact: Meta employees distributed flyers at multiple U.S. offices on Tuesday May 12, 2026 protesting the company's installation of mouse-tracking software on their computers, encouraging staff to sign an online petition against the move.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta employees distributed flyers at multiple U.S. offices on Tuesday to protest the company's recent installation of mouse-tracking software on their computers, according to photos of the pamphlets seen by Reuters. The flyers, which appeared in meeting rooms, on vending machines and atop toilet paper dispensers at the Facebook owner's offices, encouraged staffers to sign an online petition against the move.

key_facts.fact: The internal program is named the Model Capability Initiative (MCI) and was first reported by Reuters on April 22, 2026; it records mouse movements, click locations, keystrokes, keyboard shortcuts, dropdown menu navigation, and periodic screenshots on employees' work computers.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta will start tracking employees' screens and keystrokes to train AI tools, in a program internally referred to as the Model Capability Initiative (MCI). The tracking tool records mouse movements, click locations, keystrokes, keyboard shortcuts, dropdown menu navigation, and periodic screenshots.

key_facts.fact: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth told employees there is no way to disable the MCI tracking on corporate laptops, replying internally: 'There is no option to opt out on your corporate laptop.'
key_facts.excerpt: Employees immediately condemned the initiative, calling it a privacy violation, and asked whether they could turn off the tracking, to which the company's CTO, Andrew Bosworth, responded, saying, 'There is no option to opt out on your corporate laptop.'

key_facts.fact: The list of sites and applications MCI tracks includes Google, LinkedIn, Wikipedia, Microsoft GitHub, Salesforce Slack, Atlassian, and Meta's own properties such as Threads.
key_facts.excerpt: CNBC obtained a list of tracked websites and applications. The list includes Google, LinkedIn, Wikipedia, Microsoft's GitHub, Salesforce's Slack, Atlassian, and Meta's own properties like Threads and Manus.

key_facts.fact: Meta plans to lay off about 10% of its workforce — roughly 8,000 employees — starting May 20, 2026, and is scrapping plans to hire for 6,000 currently open roles, as the company pushes deeper into AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta plans to lay off 10% of its workforce, about 8,000 employees, as it continues ramping up investments in artificial intelligence, with cuts beginning May 20. The company is scrapping plans to hire people for 6,000 open roles.

key_facts.fact: Meta said in March 2026 that it would cut about 20% of its staff by the end of the year to offset rising AI infrastructure costs, with another wave of layoffs planned for the second half of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta said another wave of layoffs were planned for the second half of the year, and the company previously announced in March it would cut about 20% of its staff by the end of the year to offset AI costs.

key_facts.fact: Meta defended MCI by saying its AI agents need real examples of how people use computers — mouse movements, button clicks, dropdown navigation — to learn to complete everyday tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: "If we're building agents to help people complete everyday tasks using computers, our models need real examples of how people actually use them — things like mouse movements, clicking buttons, and navigating dropdown menus," it said.

key_facts.fact: In the UK, a group of Meta employees launched a unionization drive with United Tech and Allied Workers (UTAW), a branch of the Communication Workers Union, recruiting members through a site using the URL 'Leanin.uk' — a reference to former COO Sheryl Sandberg's book.
key_facts.excerpt: In the UK, a group of Meta employees has started organizing a drive for unionization with United Tech and Allied Workers (UTAW), a branch of the Communication Workers Union. The employees set up a website to recruit members using the URL 'Leanin.uk,' a reference to former Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg's best-selling book.

key_facts.fact: The pamphlets and petition both cite the U.S. National Labor Relations Act, stating that 'workers are legally protected when they choose to organize for the improvement of working conditions.'
key_facts.excerpt: The pamphlets and the petition both cite the U.S. National Labor Relations Act, saying "workers are legally protected when they choose to organize for the improvement of working conditions."
